newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW - Malaysia Utama sees 30 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Malaysia Utama sees 30 pct profit growth.

text.p: Soon-to-be-listed Utama Banking Group Bhd is targeting 30 percent growth a year in pre-tax profit over the next three years.
For the year ended December 31, 1996, the group recorded pre-tax profit of 87.4 million ringgit ($34.7 million), up 65.8 percent from 1995.

"The performance of the Malaysian economy is looking very favourable. Therefore to meet the 30 percent growth target is within our reach," Utama Banking chairman Nik Hashim Nik Yusoff told Reuters in an interview late on Friday.

He said the group's commercial banking arm, Bank Utama (Malaysia) Bhd, would continue to be the main profit contributor. The commercial bank, which is pursuing Tier-1 status, contributed about 75 percent to the group's 1996 pre-tax profit.
"It will still be the main contributor but the percentage may not remain at 75 percent, maybe around 60 percent, as the other businesses will also be contributing," Nik Hashim said.
He said Bank Utama hoped to achieve Tier-1 status by this year. "I think we are able to meet the requirements," he said.
Under Malaysia's two-tier banking system, banks with Tier-1 status are allowed to operate in a more liberal environment.
Bank Utama currently has 33 branches throughout the country. "We hope to open six more branches this year," Nik Hashim said.

Apart from merchant banking and finance company operations, contribution would also come from the group's stockbroking unit, Utama Securities, which was expected to begin operations early next year, he said.

Utama Merchant Bank made 24.2 million ringgit pre-tax profit in 1996, up from 18.5 million in 1995, while finance company Kewangan Utama chalked up a profit of 0.53 million ringgit against the previous year's loss of 13.6 million.
Group assets grew by 29.7 percent to 7.18 billion ringgit in 1996, while total loans and advances rose by 14.7 percent to 3.58 billion ringgit.
Nik Hashim said Utama Banking's flotation would enable the Sarawak-based medium-sized financial group to finance its expansion into one of Malaysia's larger financial supermarkets.
Utama Banking is issuing 36.45 million shares to shareholders of Cahya Mata Sarawak Bhd at three ringgit a share and a public issue of 41.15 million shares, also at three ringgit each.
Proceeds from the issues will be used to increase the equity of its subsidiaries and as working capital.
Cahya Mata, a conglomerate also based in Sarawak state, owns 57 percent of Utama Banking but its stake will be reduced to 50.7 percent after the flotation.
Despite some analysts' view that the issue price of Utama Banking share was a bit high, Nik Hashim expressed confidence that the public issue would be well received.
"For a financial conglomerate, the price is not high and we feel there is room for it to go higher," he said.
At three ringgit per share, Utama Banking's net price earnings multiple is 21 times based on forecast net earnings per share of 14.5 cents.
Scheduled for an August 8 listing, Utama Banking will be the first banking group to be listed this year.

Nik Hashim said the group was also looking to acquire an insurance company, to complete its portfolio of financial services. "We had preliminary discussion with one or two parties but the asking price was too high," he said.
($1 = 2.52 ringgit)
